builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Improving Tail-Augmented Speculative Drafting with Hidden State Mixing and Gradient Detach
summary: HSM and HSGD replace EAGLE-3's training-time test, which simulates autoregressive drafting with extra memory and specialized attention masks; HSM instead mixes backbone and MTP hidden states during training, and HSGD stochastically detaches gradients on hidden-state and embedding pathways. Neither method adds inference cost, HSM lowers peak reserved training memory by 48% versus TTT in the reported four-step comparison, and both are implemented in Megatron-LM and NVIDIA Model Optimizer. The method can fail if the target model lacks an MTP head or EAGLE-style drafter to retrain, if the short-versus-long draft-length trade-off between HSGD and HSM is misjudged for the actual serving configuration, or if the reported acceptance-length gains do not transfer to the reader's model family.
rationale: HSM removes the training-inference mismatch without TTT's memory overhead, but the gain depends on having an MTP or EAGLE-style drafter and a compatible serving stack, so it warrants a small-scale validation run before adoption.
technique: Hidden state mixing and gradient detach for speculative drafters

claims.statement: HSM and HSGD replace EAGLE-3's training-time test, which simulates autoregressive drafting with extra memory and specialized attention masks; HSM instead mixes backbone and MTP hidden states during training, and HSGD stochastically detaches gradients on hidden-state and embedding pathways. Neither method adds inference cost, HSM lowers peak reserved training memory by 48% versus TTT in the reported four-step comparison, and both are implemented in Megatron-LM and NVIDIA Model Optimizer. The method can fail if the target model lacks an MTP head or EAGLE-style drafter to retrain, if the short-versus-long draft-length trade-off between HSGD and HSM is misjudged for the actual serving configuration, or if the reported acceptance-length gains do not transfer to the reader's model family.

HSM-based MTP boosting with a frozen backbone improves mean acceptance length by up to 52.2% over the co-trained MTP across four Nemotron models and DeepSeek-V4-Pro; HSM matches EAGLE-3 TTT acceptance with 48% lower peak reserved training memory in a four-step Qwen3-8B comparison.
